A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable and describe the same VidComposition benchmark. v1 ends after the references; v4 additionally contains supplementary Sections 7–11. The supplied content supports comparison, while not establishing when the additionally documented experiments were performed.

before.justification: v1 reports original model and human evaluations in Table 2, diagnostic experiments in Section 4, and qualitative error analyses.

after.justification: v4 retains these original evaluations and additionally reports AuroraCap results, fuller diagnostic results, and analyses of model answer distributions.

M1.justification: The benchmark construction, prediction procedure in Algorithm 1, answer matching, and random fallback are unchanged. The supplementary prompt template documents the previously referenced procedure rather than establishing a new method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 982 compiled videos and 1,706 questions across five categories and 15 tasks. The supplementary task definitions, distributions, and examples do not establish additional dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: v4 adds AuroraCap to the evaluated models in Table 2 while retaining all previous comparators. Supplementary Table 7 also includes a VILA-1.5 versus InternVL2 resolution comparison absent from v1 Table 3, although both models were evaluated elsewhere in v1.

E3.justification: Supplementary Table 7 extends the reported resolution comparison to an 8B, 16-frame group beyond Table 3's 7B groups. Table 8 labels InternVL2 resolution as Dynamic, whereas v1 Table 5 and retained v4 Table 5 specify 448. This inconsistent setting disclosure does not establish a rerun; the main scoring protocol is unchanged.

E4.justification: v4 substantially expands the diagnostics with answer-option bias analyses in Figures 9 and 14, subtask difficulty distributions in Figure 10, category-specific frame sensitivity in Figure 12, and fuller factor-analysis tables. Figure 13 adds a shot-size error case to the retained camera-movement and camera-angle cases.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The supplementary distributions are descriptive analyses, and the highlighted table differences remain performance deltas rather than uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Existing main-table scores are unchanged, including human accuracy of 86.26 and LLaVA-OneVision-72B accuracy of 63.31. v4 adds AuroraCap's 36.28 overall score and task scores, numerous previously unreported category-level diagnostic results, answer-distribution results, and another qualitative error example. These substantially expand reported outcomes without demonstrating improved performance under retained settings.

T1.justification: Algorithm 1 and the accuracy definitions in Equations 1–2 are unchanged. The supplementary task descriptions are informal explanations; no new mathematical assumptions, propositions, proofs, or derivations are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: a fine-grained video-composition benchmark, a substantial human–model performance gap, and analyses of factors affecting performance. The additional comparator and supplementary evidence do not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: Section 7 newly interprets more balanced answer predictions as associated with better performance, contrasting InternVL2-40B with InternVL2-76B and identifying stronger option bias in smaller models. The existing explanations of frame redundancy and the caveat about confounded resolution comparisons remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Sections 8–10 supply previously referenced but absent documentation: descriptions of all 15 tasks, the exact multiple-choice prompt and explanation-requesting variant, and the annotation/human-evaluation interface. This substantially improves procedural documentation without establishing implementation changes. The stated code and leaderboard access is unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 adds the AuroraCap reference supporting its new Table 2 comparison. The related-work discussion and positioning against existing benchmarks remain essentially unchanged; other citation-number shifts reflect this insertion.

P1.justification: The original section order and nearly all main-text prose are retained. v4 appends supplementary explanatory sections and an acknowledgment, adjusts emphasis, and corrects the introduction's performance-figure reference from Figure 2 to Figure 1.

P2.justification: Figures 6–14 and Tables 7–9 substantially expand the visual presentation with distribution charts, a six-panel frame analysis, an interface screenshot, another qualitative case, and fuller diagnostic tables. Some panels and rows redisplay existing evidence. Figures 1–5 remain unchanged, and Table 2 gains an AuroraCap row.

improvement.justification: v4 improves transparency by supplying the previously absent prompt, task documentation, and fuller diagnostic evidence, including useful answer-bias analyses. These gains are tempered by remaining reproducibility gaps, including the still-absent promised answer-matching implementation, and conflicting InternVL2 resolution labels. The additions support a limited overall quality improvement.
